text.p: These are the headlines selected from Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Cabinet revises offloading plan: Announcement on municipal cost-sharing timed for inclusion in budget next week.
- Child welfare changes urged: Advocate needed, coroner says.
- 10,000 more put on alert to flee: Soldiers to help top up 200 kilometres of dikes as Winnipeg alters flood plan.
- Exercise found to cut breast-cancer risk: A leisurely stroll is not going to do it.
- Mobutu to meet rebel boss: Reluctant president to talk about terms of his departure.
- Labour poised to end long rule of Tories: Victory would cap turnaround for party that long seemed out of touch with Britons.
- Black bids for rest of Southam: $922.7 million offer would give Hollinger access to news chain's cash from operations.
- Low interest rates send economy 'on a tear': GDP gains in 2 months poin to 4% annualized growth.
- Bombardier gets N.Y. subway deal worth $1.3-billion: Contract for 680 cars largest ever for firm's transport group.
- GM braces for spread of disputes with union: Flow of vital components could be hit.
- Hollinger bids $923M for rest of Southam: Conrad Black springs $23.50 a- hare surprise on stock market as he swoops to take Canada's largest newspaper company private.
- Bre-X investors mull court move over broker advice.
